Join our AI Workshop Register FREE Controversial influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were arrested in the United States after British authorities announced that they will be filing additional charges against them. According to the UK's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), Andrew Tate is facing seven more rape charges in addition to existing allegations about suspected offences like child pornography and sex trafficking. Three counts of planning or aiding trafficking for sexual exploitation, two counts of rape, and one count of sexual assault have been brought against Tristan Tate. According to the BBC, the alleged offence occurred between July 2010 and August 2017. In the past, the Tates have denied any misconduct. Malcolm McHaffie, Head of the Special Crime Division at the Crown Prosecution Service, said, "These charging decisions followed receipt of a further file of evidence from Bedfordshire Police and bring the total number of alleged victims in this case to seven.” A US Department of Justice official stated that the arrests were "pursuant to extradition proceedings," while the US Marshals confirmed to the outlet that the Tates had been detained. The brothers are dual British-US nationals, and the CPS stated in its statement that it had asked for their extradition from the US. A list of 21 charges that Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 37, will eventually face in the UK was confirmed by prosecutors in May 2025. These alleged offences are believed to have occurred between 2012 and 2016. Romanian Business News - ACTMedia :: Services | About us | Contact | RSS Home Daily Financial & banking Economic Companies Energy & Environment Romania-UK trade reaches GBP10.3 billion in 2025 Bilateral trade between the UK and Romania reached GBP 10.3 billion in 2025, up 4.9% from the previous year, according to the latest data published by the United Kingdom's Department for Business and Trade, quoted by the Romanian-British Chamber of Commerce (BRCC). British exports to Romania increased by 7% to GBP 3 billion, while imports from Romania increased by 4% to GBP 7.3 billion. Thus, Romania ranks 32nd in the ranking of UK's most important trading partners . Trade in goods continued to be supported by strong activity in industry and production. "Cars represented the main category of goods imported by the United Kingdom from Romania, to the tune of GBP 1.3 billion pounds, making up 30.4% of the total British imports of goods from Romania, after an annual increase of 18.4%. Other important categories included beverages and tobacco products, general industrial machinery and electrical equipment. British exports of goods to Romania were dominated by beverages and tobacco products, mechanical power generators and cars, which highlights the importance of already strengthened industrial supply chains and the potential for extensive sectoral cooperation," reads a BRCC press release. Also, British exports of services to Romania increased by 16.1% to GBP1.5 billion (50.5% of total UK exports to Romania). In this context, travel represented the most important category of services, with a share of 37.1% of British exports of services to Romania and 43.2% of British imports of services from Romania, followed by other services for companies and transport. "The latest figures mark a new increase in bilateral trade between the United Kingdom and Romania, confirming the positive trend in the economic relationship. The contribution of key sectors such as automotive, machinery and electrical equipment, along with the growing importance of services for companies, is particularly encouraging. These results provide a solid basis for future development and point to new opportunities for investment, innovation and sectoral partnerships. At BRCC, we will continue to connect companies, institutions and industry leaders, contributing to transforming this favourable evolution into concrete projects and long-term sustainable growth," BRCC Chairman Robert Uzuna is quoted as saying in the statement. In the British foreign direct investment segment in Romania, the stock stood at GBP 752 million at the end of 2024, down 19.9% year-on-year, indicating an opportunity to strengthen investment projects and long-term capital commitment. In contrast, Romanian and UK foreign direct investment increased by 22.2% to GBP 303 million. "Romania's overall economic trajectory reinforces its growing importance in the European landscape. The country's gross domestic product is estimated to reach USD 480.8 billion in 2026, which would place Romania 39th in the ranking of the world's largest economies. It is estimated that export activity supported approximately 2.6 million jobs in Romania in 2022, of which approximately 103,600 were supported by exports to the United Kingdom. The United Kingdom's market share in Romania stood at 2.2% in 2024, indicating additional expansion potential, especially in automotive, advanced manufacturing, industrial machinery, electrical equipment, business services and technology. The combination of the already consolidated industrial supply chains and the growing services component provide a solid basis for the development of a deeper and more integrated economic relationship between Romania and the United Kingdom," according to the organisation. The Romanian-British Chamber of Commerce is the main organisation dedicated to the promotion of bilateral trade and investment between the UK and Romania. Founded in 1998, the entity operates independently and has offices in London, Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca. Oil on canvas. Courtesy of the artist and Karma International, Zurich © Kateryna Lysovenko. VIENNA .- In the MAK exhibition Kateryna Lysovenko: Borderland (16.9.2026–18.10.2026), the Ukrainian-born, Vienna-based artist Kateryna Lysovenko combines the language of classical painting with contemporary issues. In paintings—some of which were created specifically for the MAK—and selected watercolors, Lysovenko juxtaposes vulnerable bodies, hybrid beings, and mythological tales with heroic narratives of war. She investigates the connections between the body and ideology, using the medium of painting to make life in war and exile a tangible experience. With her thematic explorations, she opens up spaces for social and political imagination. Lysovenko views painting as a social act and a political medium. Her work is less about illustrating events than about methods of discovering and questioning the world. Her dynamic imagery is based on observations, shifts, and fragments of everyday life. Here, painting becomes a tool to renegotiate visibility and reality. She develops series of large-scale paintings in oil or acrylic on canvas, or as watercolors on paper. In her painting, Kateryna Lysovenko works with reduction and voids, interpreting coloration as its own resonant space. Starting from black-and-white works on paper, the artist eventually developed an assertive, polychrome formal language within an academic system she experienced as repressive. In her nuanced interplay of colors, Lysovenko uses milky shades of gray and green, bright blues, and intense reds, oranges, and pinks. They revolve around love, energy, and danger, symbolizing blood, life, and death, or signaling fire. The watercolors, on the other hand, are characterized by a subtle color palette. In her works, the artist emphasizes a shift in reality, vividly portraying situations of affected people and imaginary scenes of events. In the paintings created specifically for the MAK, Lysovenko focuses on the rivers Dnipro in Kyiv and Danube in Vienna, both of which shape a city and flow into the Black Sea as metaphors for political landscapes. They run through the pictures like veins, borders, and scars, carrying memories. Occasionally, islands serve as places of refuge and symbolize relics of the past. The flowing water and the waves of the sea symbolize migration and the shifting of political history, standing for community and solidarity. Figures are at the center of Lysovenko’s paintings and watercolors. For example, the work Kassandra sees Troy (2025) shows the protagonist amidst the landscape spreading out before her. The painting Home came at you (2024) portrays an overwhelmed woman sitting at a table while the room dissolves into a war scenario. Serving as a kind of memorial, sleeping figures in a forest feature in the painting Still Hour (2025). Wrapped in sleeping bags and crouching, the soldiers or civilians look like cocoons and mummies. In the periphery, the fringes of the forest seem to extend into infinity. The figures in Lysovenko’s paintings are in a constant state of transformation. Appearing translucent, they emerge as round shapes and embryonic bodies that weave through her imagery. The artist captures the humanity of her subjects in particular and portrays—in contrast to Socialist Realism—de-heroicized bodies, chimeras, and organisms that do not represent victims but acts of resistance, underscoring the vulnerability of the citizens. Kateryna Lysovenko (*1989, Kyiv, Ukraine) fled to Austria in 2022 and is among the most significant emerging painters of the younger generation. She studied at the Odesa Grekov Art Professional College as well as at the National Academy of Fine Arts and Architecture (NAFAA) in Kyiv. Her exhibitions have been held at venues including the CAC Contemporary Art Centre in Vilnius (2026), the Salzburger Kunstverein (2026), the Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw (2025), and the Kunstverein Hannover (2025). She is currently featured at Manifesta 16 Ruhr. The occasion for the MAK exhibition is the Münze Österreich Prize, awarded by the Austrian Mint, which Kateryna Lysovenko received in context of the viennacontemporary 2025. https://english.radio.cz/thalia-awards-b.text: CS DE EN ES FR РУ УК Thalia Awards to be presented at Prague’s National Theatre Facebook Twitter The Thalia Awards will be presented to 20 laureates at Prague’s National Theatre on Saturday evening. The awards recognise outstanding stage performances in Czech theatre in drama, opera, ballet, dance and physical theatre, as well as musicals, operettas and related genres, this time for performances between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026. Since 2020, the awards have also recognised outstanding stage performances in alternative and puppet theatre as separate categories. The organisers, the Actors’ Association, announced in mid-September that the Thalia Award for lifetime artistic achievement will go to Brno-based actress and teacher Zdena Herfortová, long-time Činoherní klub actor Petr Nárožný, former State Opera soloist Luděk Vele, ballet master and former National Theatre ballet soloist Nelly Danko, and, in the musical and dramatic genres, Studio Ypsilon ensemble member Jaroslava Kretschmerová. The Thalia Award consists of a glass sculpture made by the Ajeto Lindava glassworks. https://www.politico.eu/article/european.text: PARIS — Top European defense ministers and EU representatives said Ukraine faces challenging months ahead, insisting they must keep supporting Kyiv despite the U.S. bid for talks with Russia. "The new diplomatic push is there, but it's also clear that Putin's actions tell a different story," the EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said at a press conference in Paris on Monday. Kallas said she was expecting a "brutal winter" for Kyiv and that there was "no hope for imminent peace," reiterating the need to help Ukraine "withstand the attacks and increase the cost for Russia." Kallas, along with European Commissioner for Defence and Space Andrius Kubilius, joined a meeting with defense ministers from the E5 group made up of France, the U.K., Germany, Poland and Italy, hosted at the French armed forces ministry. Advertisement Advertisement The meeting came amid a renewed U.S. effort to push Ukraine into peace talks with Russia and growing doubts about Washington's support for Kyiv. U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff said last week he would offer Russia's Vladimir Putin direct talks with President Donald Trump and Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy to secure a ceasefire. "No results whatsoever comes for those who want to negotiate with Putin," German defense minister Boris Pistoripus said. "The results are what? It doesn't lead to anything. There is no signal whatsoever that Putin is looking for peace." The U.K.'s Wes Streeting added: "While none of us seek confrontation with Russia ... We do have to be aware of the threat posed by Russia." While pledging "total transparency" with the U.S., France's Catherine Vautrin said the E5 members would "work together concretely," focusing on arms production and interoperability. "Produce more, produce faster, produce equipment suited to today’s conflicts – but we must already be planning for the conflicts of tomorrow," Vautrin said. "On that, EU financial initiatives can help us move in this direction." Advertisement Advertisement
